questions: Should the output be a plain integer count, or should it be taken modulo some value (e.g., 10^9+7) as is common in competitive programming problems?
Are the integers in S guaranteed to be sorted in increasing order in the input, or can they appear in any order?
Is the condition B - A = C - B strictly about the arithmetic difference, or does it also imply something about the positions/indexes of A, B, C in the set S?
If N is up to 10^6, is an O(N^2) solution acceptable, or must it be more efficient like O(N log N)?
Can A, B, C be any three distinct elements from S, or must they appear in the order A < B < C as per the condition?
Should the count include triplets where B - A = C - B = 0, given that A, B, C are distinct positive integers?
Is the output required to be a 64-bit integer (e.g., long long in C++) to avoid overflow, given N up to 10^6 could produce large counts?
Are there any constraints on the memory usage or specific algorithms that should be avoided?
